id: ml-02
title: TabNet
paper: Arik & Pfister, TabNet: Attentive Interpretable Tabular Learning (arXiv Aug 2019; AAAI 2021)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.07442
type: Benchmark
cutoff: 2019-08-20
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Refuted as a general superiority claim; narrowly supported on its own datasets. In Shwartz-Ziv & Armon's rerun, TabNet slightly beats XGBoost on the three TabNet-paper datasets (Rossmann, CoverType, Higgs) but loses on most others. XGBoost wins 8 of 11 datasets overall and needs much less tuning. Grinsztajn et al. find tree models remain state of the art on medium-sized tabular data. The verdict must not inherit a blanket "refuted" without that nuance.

## I0
Can an attentive tabular network improve prediction and useful feature selection?

## evidence
- Architecture: sequential attentive feature selection with sparsemax masks per decision step; instance-wise interpretability; optional masked self-supervised pretraining.
- Results: Forest Cover Type accuracy 96.99% vs XGBoost 89.34, LightGBM 89.28, CatBoost 85.14, AutoML Tables 94.95 (Table 2); Poker Hand: XGBoost 70.0, LightGBM 66.6 vs TabNet higher (Table 3); Sarcos MSE TabNet-M 0.14 vs MLP 1.23, random forest 2.39 (Table 4); synthetic feature-selection tasks Syn1–6 on par with INVASE (Table 1).
- Claim: outperforms on "non-performance-saturated" tabular datasets; a single TabNet "without fine-grained hyperparameter search" beats tuned AutoML.
- Tree baselines described as "tuned"; tuning budgets not reported in comparable detail.

## intake
- Scope: (A) TabNet beats tree ensembles on selected tabular benchmarks; (B) its masks give useful feature attributions.
- Regime: a handful of large datasets (Forest Cover, Poker Hand, Sarcos, Higgs, Rossmann); author-chosen splits.
- Assumptions: dataset selection is representative; baselines tuned with equal effort; masks reflect true feature importance.
- Falsifiers: tuned XGBoost/CatBoost matching or beating TabNet on these and other datasets; masks failing ground-truth feature recovery.

## screen
- Must flag: dataset selection ("non-performance-saturated"); unequal tuning budgets; baseline numbers partly taken from other papers; interpretability not validated against ground truth on real data.
- Must request: equal-budget hyperparameter search; a broad benchmark suite.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: XGBoost (Chen & Guestrin 2016), LightGBM, CatBoost; deep neural decision trees; L2X and INVASE feature selection; Fernández-Delgado et al. 2014 classifier survey.
- Current mode: Shwartz-Ziv & Armon 2021: XGBoost beats the deep models on 8 of 11 datasets (p < 0.005), needs less tuning; ensembles of deep models + XGBoost do best. Grinsztajn et al. 2022: 45 datasets, 20,000 compute-hours of search; trees remain SOTA on ~10K-sample data.

## designer
- Same splits for all models; equal hyperparameter-search budgets (trials or GPU-hours); ≥ 4 seeds; include datasets not chosen by the TabNet authors; test feature-selection fidelity on synthetic ground truth separately.

## champion
- Tuned XGBoost / CatBoost (and, for small data, TabPFN), matching our criterion 5.

## panel
- Flaw: dataset and tuning asymmetry. Repair: restrict the claim to the reported datasets and add an independent benchmark suite.

## run
- pytorch-tabnet + XGBoost on Forest Cover Type with equal Optuna budgets; check the 96.99 vs 89.34 gap shrinks when XGBoost is tuned.

## verdict
- Label: Refuted (general superiority); scoped support on its own datasets.
- Must say: gains are dataset-specific and do not survive broad, equal-budget benchmarks.
- Must not say: TabNet never helps; or TabNet beats tree ensembles in general.

## audit
- Check: 96.99 / 89.34 / 94.95; Shwartz-Ziv Table 2 (TabNet 3.01 vs XGBoost 3.13 on CoverType log-loss; 8 of 11 datasets); Grinsztajn 45 datasets.

## variants
- Find a reproducible regime where attention helps (very large data, many irrelevant features) with equal tuning; relevant to our TabPFN/XGBoost baseline policy.
